D.t: Rob Sand leads by 7.7 in the forecast and wins 92% of simulations. The cushion is about 105,977 votes; a one point swing is about 6,864 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +0.7 and D +14.9. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.

The polls page average is D +6.6. Your best recent poll is Cook Political Report/GS Strategy Group and New River Strategies at D +11.0; your worst is On Point Polling at D +4.7. 13 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Polk, a projected net 71,690 votes; Johnson, a projected net 43,210 votes; Linn, a projected net 33,480 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Pottawattamie, D +1.1, 2.5% of the vote; Woodbury, R +4.2, 2.5% of the vote; Warren, D +0.2, 1.9% of the vote; Clinton, D +4.1, 1.4% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Rob Sand runs furthest behind in Sioux, Marion, Webster. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 92% of voters, 51 to 47, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.62 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 72% of voters, 52 to 46, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.62 points; Voters without a degree, 64% of voters, 51 to 47, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.19 points.

The forecast's worst groups for Rob Sand: Immigration voters 24 to 74, Small counties 42 to 56, Voters who can afford daily costs 44 to 54. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
Registered Democrats cast 50% of the 286,878 ballots in Iowa so far, against 32% for the other party. That is 6.5 points worse for Democrats than the forecast expected by now.
